>
> The code-review verdict is reported AS-IS — it is **not** masked as `ai-review:changes` (#596), so a genuine reviewer-requested change on a machinery PR still surfaces distinctly. Auto-merge is held by a SEPARATE human gate instead: the `needs-human-review` label, the `machinery-review-required` check, and `ready-to-merge` staying red (no SHA-bound pass witness is posted for a machinery PR).

commits.messageBody:
…t's own issue ref

Root cause: the follow-up-gate escape ran its grep over the whole composed
message, subject line included. This repo's own conventional-commit style
puts the issue number in the subject (`feat(#N): ...`), so that number alone
satisfied the bare `#[0-9]+` escape on nearly every commit — the gate almost
never actually fired (0 blocks measured since 2026-07-27).

- Strip the subject line (first non-blank line, not just line 1) from the
  text both the deferral trigger and its escape scan, so a subject-only ref
  can no longer double as the escape.
- Replace the bare `#[0-9]+` escape with a structured `Follow-ups:` trailer,
  read via `git interpret-trailers --parse`, whose value is `#NNN[, #NNN...]`.
  The other prose escapes ("tracked in", "Follow-ups: none", "handled here",
  "nothing deferred") are unchanged.
- Regenerate this repo's self-applied copy (.minspec/hooks/commit-msg) from
  the updated template so self-application stays in sync (enforced by
  managed-region-self-application.test.ts).
- Add regression tests: a subject-only `(#N)` ref, and a bare inline `#NNN`
  mention with no trailer/escape phrase, must both still BLOCK; a
  `Follow-ups: #NNN` / `#NNN, #NNN` trailer must ALLOW.

Follow-ups: the issue also asks to port the fixed gate into this repo's own
active hook, .githooks/commit-msg (currently carries only the RCDD gate, no
follow-up gate at all — so self-application never exercises it). That file
is machinery (dispatch-issue.sh's MACHINERY_PATH_RE) and outside this dev
task's file allowlist (packages/, tests/, scripts/), so it is intentionally
not touched here. Needs a tracked issue filed by a human/dispatcher, since
this session cannot run `gh`.

commits.messageBody:
… bypassing the scissors strip

PR #2067 review (Architect: blocking, Security: independently converged): the
structured `Follow-ups:` escape ran `git interpret-trailers --parse "$msg_file"`
on the raw message file instead of the already scissors/comment-stripped
`$body` every other check in this hook uses (DR-059 §3 mandates the strip so
verbose-diff text can never influence the gate).

Root cause: the escape was written directly against `$msg_file` instead of
`$body` when the structured trailer parse was added for #1918, so it never
went through the strip the rest of the hook enforces — and no test exercised
a `git commit -v` shaped message (trailer above the scissors line, diff
below), so nothing caught the gap. Empirically verified: git's own trailer
parser has its own internal cut-line detection for the `-v` scissors marker,
and that detection is stricter/more format-sensitive than this hook's
deliberately lenient `sed '/^#.*>8/,$ d'` — a scissors line that doesn't match
git's parser byte-for-byte (confirmed with trailing whitespace and a
non-canonical dash count) makes it silently return no trailer at all, even
though a real one is present above the diff, falsely blocking a legitimate
commit.

Fix: parse trailers from `$body` (piped via stdin) in both the live hook and
its `packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts` COMMIT_MSG_HOOK mirror, so
the trailer path goes through the same strip as every other check. Also fixed
a misleading comment (non-blocking finding, same review): it implied the
`Follow-ups:` trailer itself accepts `none`, but that case is handled by the
separate prose-escape regex, not the trailer parse.

Added a failing-first regression test (packages/minspec/tests/dr037-hook-scaffolds.test.ts)
reproducing the `-v` shape with a real trailer above a scissors line whose
trailing whitespace defeats git's raw-file trailer detection; confirmed it
failed against the unfixed hook (exit 1, false block) before applying the fix,
and a negative-control test confirming the gate still blocks a genuine
untracked deferral in the same shape.

Follow-ups: none

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
